platinum.name: Platinum Age
platinum.description: Early comic strip reprints and proto-comics
common_defects: Brittle pages due to acidic paper
platinum.grading_notes: Paper quality is paramount - many Platinum Age comics used highly acidic newsprint. Expect significant browning and brittleness. Completeness is often an issue - many were stripped of covers. Restoration is common and expected.
prompt_additions: Pay special attention to paper brittleness - does it appear fragile or crumbling?
Check for signs of amateur restoration common to this era (tape, glue, trimming)
Assess page completeness - missing pages are common
Note any newsprint quality indicators
Evaluate binding method - many used different techniques than later eras

golden.name: Golden Age
golden.description: First superhero comics, including Action Comics #1
golden.grading_notes: Golden Age comics used wartime paper (1941-1945) which was particularly poor quality. Marvel/Timely comics are notorious for 'Marvel chipping'. Staple rust is extremely common. Cover gloss is a key differentiator between high grades.
prompt_additions: Carefully examine page edges for Marvel chipping or brittleness
Check staples for rust migration into surrounding paper
Assess spine stress - these comics were often rolled for storage
Look for oxidation shadow around staples on interior pages
Note paper stock - wartime issues (1942-1945) had inferior paper
Examine centerfold for detachment signs

silver.name: Silver Age
silver.description: Marvel Comics revolution, revised DC heroes
silver.grading_notes: Silver Age paper quality improved but color preservation varies greatly. Marvel value stamps and corner boxes were often clipped. Cover gloss becomes a major grading factor. Subscription copies have distinctive spine/cover wear.
prompt_additions: Check for Marvel value stamp presence (if applicable)
Examine corner boxes for clipping
Assess cover gloss retention - key for high grades
Look for subscription fold/crease patterns
Check for price stickers or distributor markings
Evaluate color vibrancy especially on key colors (red/yellow fade faster)

bronze.name: Bronze Age
bronze.grading_notes: Bronze Age introduced direct market editions with generally better preservation. Newsstand copies show more handling wear. Cover gloss is critical for 9.8+ grades. Spine stress lines are common from spinner rack display.
prompt_additions: Distinguish between newsstand and direct edition condition
Examine spine carefully for stress lines and ticks
Check cover corners for blunting
Look for reading creases especially at centerfold
Assess cover gloss - essential for Near Mint grades
Note any price variants or distribution marks

copper.name: Copper Age
copper.description: Independent comics boom, speculation era begins
copper.grading_notes: Copper Age saw introduction of better paper and printing. Manufacturing defects become more noticeable at high grades. Many comics were immediately bagged, but often with damaging non-archival materials.
prompt_additions: Check for manufacturing/bindery defects
Examine for non-archival storage damage (acid migration)
Look for color printing misregistration
Assess spine squareness - manufacturing variations exist
Check for diamond distributor damage patterns

modern.name: Modern Age
modern.description: Current era with variant covers and digital coloring
modern.grading_notes: Modern comics use high-quality paper but manufacturing tolerances create defects. Expectations for 9.8+ are extremely high. Minor defects that wouldn't affect earlier era grades become significant. White pages are expected, not exceptional.
prompt_additions: Scrutinize for even minor manufacturing defects
Check spine for any color breaking
Examine covers for fingerprints or handling marks
Look for corner dents or shipping damage
Assess centering of cover artwork
Note any variant cover specific issues (foil, die-cut, etc.)

base_grading_prompt.system: You are an expert comic book grader following CGC (Certified Guaranty Company) grading standards. Analyze the provided comic book image(s) and provide a detailed grade assessment.
instructions: Examine the cover condition including gloss, color retention, and wear
Assess structural integrity: spine, staples, binding
Note all defects with severity ratings (minor/moderate/major)
Consider the comic's era when evaluating condition
Provide a numeric grade from 0.5 to 10.0 on the CGC scale
List specific defects that influenced the grade
Note any signs of restoration or cleaning

grade_scale.10.0: Gem Mint - Perfect in every way
grade_scale.9.9: Mint - Near perfect with minuscule defects
grade_scale.9.8: Near Mint/Mint - Nearly perfect, minor manufacturing defects only
grade_scale.9.6: Near Mint+ - Very minor cover/interior flaws
grade_scale.9.4: Near Mint - Minor wear beginning to show
grade_scale.9.2: Near Mint- - Slight cover wear, small defects
grade_scale.9.0: Very Fine/Near Mint - Some wear, minor creasing
grade_scale.8.5: Very Fine+ - Minor wear, small creases
grade_scale.8.0: Very Fine - Minor wear, possible small creases
grade_scale.7.5: Very Fine- - Moderate wear, possible creases
grade_scale.7.0: Fine/Very Fine - Some wear, light creases
grade_scale.5.5: Fine- - Above average with noticeable wear
grade_scale.4.5: Very Good+ - Below average, multiple defects
grade_scale.4.0: Very Good - Significant wear, still complete
grade_scale.3.5: Very Good- - Heavy wear, all pages present
grade_scale.2.5: Good+ - Heavy wear, possible pieces missing
grade_scale.2.0: Good - Extensive wear, tape repairs possible
grade_scale.1.5: Fair/Good - Extremely worn, possible missing pieces
grade_scale.1.0: Fair - Heavily damaged but still mostly complete
grade_scale.0.5: Poor - Barely readable, major pieces missing
